keyconfounds: Native column kernel never stores outputrow0; GPU resetzero retained. Original CPU writes that row while original GPU verifier excludes radiusborder. Full native-output equivalence is not ideal-box-filter boundary correctness.
Horizontal zero padding differs from vertical edge replication; RGBA8 quantization occurs between passes.
JACC shared template90UInt32 preload and extra initialization barrier are measured overhead absent in native/CUDA.jl/KA.
Only synthetic256x128radius10 fixture; PPM decoding and otherimage dimensions unmeasured.

scientific_intent.scientific_task: Apply a separable21x21 box smoothing operation to packed RGBA images.
scientific_intent.mathematical_operation: Per-channel horizontal21-sample average quantized to8bits, followed by vertical21-sample sliding average quantized again.
scientific_intent.discretization_or_topology: 2D image lattice with radius10 stencil; horizontal zero-extension and vertical edge replication.
invariants: Uniform interior colors retained modulo integer quantization.
Channels processed independently; alpha participates as a fourth color channel.
accuracy_requirements: All32768 packed pixels must agree exactly with native GPU and repaired CUDA.jl outputs.
Independent Julia CPU direct stencil and native CPU oracle use an explicit row0zero policy to match native observable defect.
Original unmasked CPU boundary correctness is separately reported, not silently certified.
scientific_intent.precision_sensitivity: Float32 sums of8bit channel integers then reciprocal21 scaling/truncation. Intermediate8bit quantization is semantically required; replacing it with fullprecision convolution changes results.
scientific_intent.input_size_regimes: Synthetic256x128 packed image, radius10, ten internalrepeats; original PPM workloads not newlymeasured.
scientific_intent.community_use_case: Image smoothing primitive from NVIDIA sample source. No particular medical, astronomical or other scientific image dataset is identified.
scientific_intent.uncertainty: Native firstrow defect limits application-level mathematical correctness despite complete source-output equivalence.
